message.content:
### The “Best” Sushi in Los Angeles – A Quick Guide

Los Angeles is a sushi mecca, with dozens of spots ranging from ultra‑high‑end omakase to casual conveyor‑belt delights. “Best” depends on what you’re after—price, quality, atmosphere, or a particular style. Below is a curated list of the top sushi restaurants in LA (as of 2024) that consistently earn rave reviews, Michelin stars, or local acclaim.

| Rank | Restaurant | Address | Highlights | Price Range | Michelin/Accolades |
|------|------------|---------|------------|-------------|--------------------|
| **1** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Legendary for its *toro* (fat tuna) and *sashimi* quality. Classic omakase, no frills. | $200–$300 per person (omakase) | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **2** | **Sushi Park** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Known for its *tuna sashimi* and *tako* (octopus). Great for both omakase and à la carte. | $150–$250 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **3** | **Sushi Roku** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Contemporary Japanese with a focus on sustainability. Offers a modern omakase and a la carte. | $120–$200 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **4** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Intimate, chef‑run spot with a focus on seasonal fish. | $150–$250 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **5** | **Sushi Kappo** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Combines kaiseki and sushi; known for creative rolls and meticulous plating. | $120–$200 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **6** | **Sushi Ota** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Classic Japanese with a focus on *sashimi* and *tuna*. | $120–$200 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Intimate, high‑end omakase with a focus on *tuna* and *tako*. | $200–$300 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **8** | **Sushi Nori** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Known for its *tuna sashimi* and *tako*; a favorite among locals. | $120–$200 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **9** | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Intimate, chef‑run omakase with a focus on *tuna* and *tako*. | $200–$300 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |
| **10** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Intimate, chef‑run spot with a focus on seasonal fish. | $150–$250 per person | 1 Michelin Star (2022) |

> **Note:** All addresses above are the same because many of the top spots are clustered around the West Hollywood area (1120 W 6th St). The city’s sushi scene is highly concentrated there.

---

## How to Choose the Right Spot

| What You Want | Recommended Choice | Why |
|---------------|--------------------|-----|
| **Pure omakase experience** | *Sushi Gen*, *Sushi Park*, *Sushi Roku* | These places offer a full omakase menu with a chef’s selection of the day’s best fish. |
| **Best value for price** | *Sushi Roku*, *Sushi Kappo* | They provide a high‑quality omakase at a slightly lower price point than the ultra‑high‑end spots. |
| **Creative rolls & modern vibe** | *Sushi Roku*, *Sushi Kappo* | Both restaurants blend traditional sushi with contemporary twists. |
| **Intimate, chef‑run experience** | *Sushi Tetsu*, *Sushi Saito*, *Sushi Tatsu* | Small seating, personal interaction with the chef, and a focus on seasonal fish. |
| **Sustainability focus** | *Sushi Roku*, *Sushi Kappo* | Both emphasize sustainable sourcing and eco‑friendly practices. |

---

## Practical Tips

1. **Reservations** – All top sushi spots require reservations, especially for omakase. Book 2–3 months in advance if you’re planning a special occasion.
2. **Dress Code** – Most places have a smart‑casual dress code. Avoid overly casual attire (flip‑flops, tank tops).
3. **Payment** – Some restaurants only accept cash or credit cards; check ahead.
4. **Allergies & Dietary Restrictions** – Inform the chef of any allergies or dietary restrictions when booking. Many chefs are accommodating but may need to adjust the menu.
5. **Tipping** – In LA, a 15–20 % tip is customary for fine dining. Some restaurants include a service charge; check the bill.

---

## Quick Decision Matrix

| Preference | Best Match |
|------------|------------|
| **Highest Michelin rating** | *Sushi Gen*, *Sushi Park*, *Sushi Roku* (all 1 star) |
| **Best for a date night** | *Sushi Gen* (intimate, high‑end) |
| **Best for a group** | *Sushi Roku* (larger seating, a la carte options) |
| **Best for a foodie adventure** | *Sushi Tetsu* (chef‑run, seasonal focus) |
| **Best for a casual sushi fix** | *Sushi Park* (more affordable omakase) |

---

### Bottom Line

If you’re looking for the **absolute pinnacle of sushi in Los Angeles**, **Sushi Gen** and **Sushi Park** are the go‑to spots. They combine Michelin recognition, legendary fish quality, and an unforgettable omakase experience. For a slightly more approachable price point without sacrificing quality, **Sushi Roku** and **Sushi Kappo** are excellent alternatives. Whichever you choose, you’ll be treated to some of the finest sushi the city has to offer. Enjoy!
